label: early original-phase steps after a prefix rich in h/x/e/f/d/b/3/1
explanation: Fires mostly (79% of mass) in the original phase at positions 2-5, never at t=0, rarely on the delimiter. It fires when the prefix read so far is dominated by tokens from {h,x,e,f,d,b,3,1} (prev_tok x gives 3.6x lift; prev2_tok h/x/e also high; first_tok h/f/x/e/d/b), and the current input t/o/x/a gives extra lift. Top examples, e.g. h x h [x], b 3 h [d h x], have an h/x-heavy prefix. It weakens after position 6 and is weak in the copy phase, where it fires on about 3% of steps (prev outputs h/b/f). The rule (positions 2-6, at least half of the prefix from that set) gets dev F1 0.375, precision 0.30, mass recall 0.62. The activation looks like a distributed linear readout of the token history, so a boolean rule captures only part of it. Magnitude is largest at t=2-3 with an x/h prefix. I did not check magnitude claims beyond this.
